ic_name: IEEE 1149.1 JTAG TAP Controller (TI SSYA002C primer)

registers.name: IR
registers.access: Shift-in / shift-out via TDI / TDO in ShiftIR; parallel-latched to current-instruction on falling edge of TCK in UpdateIR.
registers.reset_value: IDCODE opcode (if Device Identification Register is implemented) OR BYPASS opcode (all 1s) otherwise
registers.purpose: Holds the currently active instruction. The instruction selects which Data Register is connected between TDI and TDO in ShiftDR and determines the test mode (BYPASS / EXTEST / SAMPLE/PRELOAD / INTEST / IDCODE / USERCODE / HIGHZ / CLAMP / RUNBIST).
registers.capture_value_in_CaptureIR: Spec-mandated fixed pattern 'b...b01' — the two LSBs are loaded with '01' so the tester can verify the IR is functioning by shifting it out and checking the bottom two bits.
registers.notes: All-1s opcode is reserved for BYPASS so that an open / pull-up-defaulted TDI naturally selects BYPASS rather than EXTEST (which would drive the board).

registers.name: Bypass
registers.access: Shift-in / shift-out via TDI / TDO in ShiftDR (when BYPASS / CLAMP / HIGHZ is current).
registers.reset_value: 0 in CaptureDR (Bypass register loads 0 in CaptureDR before each shift)
registers.purpose: 1-bit short-cut between TDI and TDO. Used to reduce daisy-chain shift length when a device is not being targeted by the current test.

registers.name: BSR
registers.width_bits: 1 BSC per external I/O pin (sum of input cells + output cells + bidir cells + control cells); implementation- and pin-count-dependent
registers.access: Shift-in / shift-out via TDI / TDO in ShiftDR (when SAMPLE/PRELOAD / EXTEST / INTEST is current).
registers.reset_value: Not specified by IEEE 1149.1 at the protocol layer; entry into TestLogicReset returns to functional operation so the BSR is don't-care.
registers.purpose: Provides observability + controllability of every external I/O pin. Each boundary-scan cell (BSC) typically contains a capture flip-flop + an update flip-flop + a 2-to-1 mux selecting either functional data or BSR drive data. Per-pin cells: input cell (observe only), output cell (drive + observe), bidir cell (drive + observe + direction control), control cell (drives the OE / direction of an associated bidir cell).
registers.structure_summary: BSR width = pin_count_summed_per_cell_type. See L17 for the per-pin BSC catalog.

registers.name: IDCODE
registers.access: Shift-out via TDO in ShiftDR (when IDCODE / USERCODE is current). The register is parallel-loaded with the device ID in CaptureDR; shifted contents into TDI are typically ignored.
registers.reset_value: Fixed at silicon mask level: version[31:28] || part-number[27:12] || manufacturer-id[11:1] || 1[0]
registers.purpose: 32-bit device fingerprint, readable by the tester to confirm which device is in each slot of the daisy chain.

field_map.name: lsb_one
field_map.description: Hard-wired to 1 so that a device with IDCODE selected is distinguishable on TDO from a device with BYPASS selected (whose Bypass register loads 0 in CaptureDR).

base_address: Defined at SoC level; offsets given relative to module base.
notes: Per IEEE 1149.1, the IR is the only register parallel-latched in UpdateIR; the Bypass register is parallel-loaded with 0 in CaptureDR; the BSR's CaptureDR behavior depends on the cell type (input cells capture pin value, output cells capture driven value); the Device Identification register is parallel-loaded with the hard-wired ID in CaptureDR.
register_map_kind: shift-register catalog (not memory-mapped). Registers are selected implicitly by the current Instruction Register value and are accessed by shifting bit-serially via TDI/TDO in ShiftIR / ShiftDR states.
selection_rule: The current Instruction Register value selects which Data Register is connected between TDI and TDO during ShiftDR / CaptureDR / UpdateDR. Instruction-to-register mapping is implementation-defined except for the protocol-mandated cases: BYPASS / CLAMP / HIGHZ → Bypass; SAMPLE/PRELOAD / EXTEST / INTEST → BSR; IDCODE / USERCODE → Device Identification Register.
user_defined_data_registers: Optional. Vendor-specific registers (e.g. configuration shift in FPGAs, flash-programming registers, internal scan paths, USERCODE) are also IR-selected. The TAP controller and IR support arbitrary user-defined data registers as long as the standard shift / capture / update mechanism is preserved.
